utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, in your opinion, is the significance of the JNA operating without the assistance of Serb paramilitaries or local forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It indicates that the JNA had objectives of its own, that it was not simply being led by local Serbian populations in particular areas. In particular, the operation in that area I think also begins to indicate the nature of the war and the project which is being fought for. The Yugoslav Navy was sailing up the coast destroying houses, people were fleeing from most of that area very quickly, within the space of around two weeks, the JNA forces using Montenegrin, reservist from Montenegro, to supplement had moved up and occupied the whole of that strip of coast with the exception of Dubrovnik. That siege and the operations in those areas indicate to me that the aim of the JNA, as part of this project, was to create territories in which there would be no alien populations, that is, no populations which would oppose being part of the borders of this new Yugoslavia, the project for which the JNA, in conjunction with Serbian political leadership, was fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any political action taken parallel with the military operation of the JNA in the latter part of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? I did not hear the whole of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any political action taken parallel with the military operation of the JNA in the latter part of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through from 1990 onwards, political action relevant to the project I identify was taking place. In particular, on 21st December 1990, the two Serbian autonomous provinces which had already been declared, that is, the Serbian autonomous region of Krajina, the territory designated here, and Serbian autonomous province of Eastern Slovenia, Baranja and Western Srem, this one here, had been united into one Serbian autonomous province. On February 28th, 1991, this territory had proclaimed a provisional constitution for a Republic of Serbian Krajina, and on 19th December 1991 that constitution was put into effect with a declaration of the Republic of Serbian Krajina; so that was to say that the territories marked as part of this area would be no longer part of the Republic of Croatia, but would be the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and the idea, I think, was that Republic of Serbian Krajina would form part, would be one element in the new mini Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with that political action, would you look, please, at the document that you are now shown. Can you tell us what the document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an English language translation of the constitution to which I just made reference of the Republic of Serbian Krajina declared by Serbs in control of those areas in Croatia in 1991. It appears in the series Constitutions of Dependencies and Special Sovereignties in the Oceana publication series to which a reference has already been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it contain the declaration which you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It contains the text of the constitution of the Republic of Serbian Krajina as implemented as I see, according to this, from February 1991. I think I said the wrong date before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honour, document 44.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there objection to 44?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 44 will be admitted. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Dr. Gow, I think that you have already touched upon the success or otherwise of the JNA campaign in Croatia, but did the JNA fulfil its objective in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It certainly did not fulfil its objectives as expressed by Generals Kadijevic and Panic with regard to Croatia as a whole. It did not, according to the same Generals, again achieve its aims within the terms of the first phase of operations, the limited operations, with regard to the areas in which there would be a strong element of a Serbian population. Both Generals made reference to the failure of the JNA and its associates within this project to accomplish their aims in western Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following this lack of success in Slovenia and Croatia by the end of 1991, did the JNA aim for a lesser objective in terms of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may clarify, as I was just indicating, when the JNA's -- I would judge that the JNA's original objective in June 1991 was to try to preserve the SFRY as a whole, and when it deployed troops on the borders, border posts between Slovenia/Italy, Slovenia/Austria, and so forth, that was probably its intention. I cannot say that that is the case for certain; it is my interpretation of that situation. I would say that after that, some of the evidence that we have seen, the words of Generals Kadijevic and Panic, in particular, indicate that it fell back on the objective of trying to keep Croatia, but not Slovenia, within some kind of renewed federal arrangement, some renewed Yugoslavia, and when that, it became clear to them that their resources would not permit to them achieve that objective, they fell back on the establishment of new borders largely based around Serbian populations, in this case in Croatia, as would be the case after that at some time in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there references to these particular matters that you have just attested to in the book by General Kadijevic which is Prosecution Exhibit 30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the consequences for Bosnia following activities of the JNA in Croatia in the latter part of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann, I think you may be moving into a new area?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Perhaps now is a good time to adjourn for the evening. Let me remind the parties that tomorrow we will adjourn at 4.00, a little bit earlier than usual, because there is another matter that has to be taken up by this Trial Chamber. So we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m.
